chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
title: Touring the West with Sarah; Storyville in Boston
summary: The trio plays the Blue Note, California, Kansas City and Omaha, then the Apollo, Baltimore, the Howard and George Wein's Storyville.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: So with these two guys, it turns out that I was in another happy situation as an accompanist to Sarah, as well as playing with some good guys as trio members. And we traveled... We went to California.. Again, we wound up with at least two engagements in the Blue Note that year. Of course, the Blue Note had... I think from the last time we'd played there, it had changed locations to a bigger place.

Let's see, from Kansas City to... We played Omaha, Nebraska/ California -- Los Angeles, San Francisco. Kansas City. Then we just played points west... It was just a very good, happy tour to work with, this gig with Sarah and Roy and Joe Benjamin.

When we got back to New York, I think we played the Apollo Theatre, and then we played a theatre in Baltimore, and then Washington D.C. at the Howard Theatre. And we went to Boston to play Storyville, which had been another one of our

yearly places where Sarah played quite a bit. At that particular time, Storyville had been in another location, another one of those squares in Boston... It was over by the ballpark there -- I can't remember that square right now. But it had moved to Copley Square. George Wein was, of course, the proprietor. And we had had quite a few successful engagements there.
